requestedActions.title: Authorize the app for each individual connected account via OAuth
List file and folder names in the connected account's App Folder, including continuation until all entries are listed

prohibitions: Upload, edit, move, or delete files or folders
guide.summary: Dropbox documents user OAuth 2.0 with the code flow and PKCE for individual accounts, with access tokens sent as Bearer headers. The app must be registered in the App Console with an app key, secret and redirect URIs, and its file access set to App Folder. The list_folder and list_folder/continue endpoints require files.metadata.read and support cursor pagination. The snapshots do not cover distribution to other customer organizations, so that remains unknown.

findings.title: User OAuth code flow is the documented path for individual account authorization
findings.detail: Dropbox documents the code flow as recommended for all application types. The app builds an authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code, then exchanges the returned code at /oauth2/token for a token used in API calls.
findings.appliesWhen: Each connected individual customer account authorizes the app through OAuth.

evidence.quote: is the recommended OAuth flow for all types of applications. In order to implement it, your application should:
Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user
Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

findings.title: Scoped user tokens are associated with the authorizing user
findings.detail: Apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token associated with the user who authorizes the app. The Authorization header carries that token as Bearer. This matches the requested per-account access without team administration.
findings.appliesWhen: The app requests only user-level scopes and does not use team administration.

evidence.quote: Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.
be used by your app in subsequent API calls for that user. It should be passed with the Authorization HTTP header value of Bearer <oauth2-access-token>
Using User and Team Tokens

findings.title: files.metadata.read is the required scope for listing folder entries
findings.detail: The list_folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read and accepts a user OAuth token. The list_folder/continue endpoint uses the same required scope, so both continue listing the App Folder with one grant.
findings.appliesWhen: Calls to list_folder and list_folder/continue list file and folder names in the connected account's App Folder.

evidence.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
list_folder . Required scope: files.metadata.read

findings.title: App Folder file access must be selected when creating the app
findings.detail: Dropbox asks for the file access scope at app creation. App Folder limits actions to data within the app folder, under /apps, which fits the requirement to list entries only in the App Folder.
findings.appliesWhen: The app is created in the App Console and connected accounts must be limited to the App Folder.

evidence.quote: App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable for
your Dropbox application, you will also be prompted to select the scope of file access. Currently, these two options are:
apps that export content or manage only their content.

findings.title: App registration with redirect URIs is required before the first test
findings.detail: The app must be registered in the App Console to obtain an app key and secret. Each redirect URI the app may use must be registered there, because Dropbox checks the redirect_uri at authorization time.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first OAuth authorization test for connected accounts.

steps.title: List the first page of App Folder entries
steps.detail: Call list_folder with path set to the empty string to list the root of the App Folder, without recursion. Read only; do not request content.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns entries (names and types), a cursor and has_more. Output is file and folder names only. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
Response Successful response cursor string >=1 character

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from exchange-authorization-code response
path: empty string means the App Folder root
limit: optional page size 1-2000

steps.title: Continue listing App Folder entries until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the latest cursor and accumulate entry names. Stop only when has_more is false. Do not invent a cursor or assume an early stop. Use the cursor from the most recent response and repeat until has_more is false. Only file and folder names are collected.
steps.doneWhen: Repeated continue calls return has_more=false and all entry names have been collected. has_more is false in the latest response; the full App Folder listing is complete. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
